risks.title: Persistent Inflation and Monetary Policy Tightening
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above the 2% target, forcing central banks, particularly the Federal Reserve, to continue raising interest rates. This tightening cycle risks slowing economic growth and increasing borrowing costs.
risks.watch_for: FOMC statements and Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) indicating future rate hikes; core PCE inflation data; wage and housing inflation trends.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes, September 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 2026)
Federal Reserve (Summary of Economic Projections, September 2026)
KPMG (Inflation Forces the Fed's Hand, September 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Fragmentation and Trade Tensions
risks.summary: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts and rising trade tensions, including tariffs, are redrawing alliances, rerouting trade, and increasing supply chain costs and uncertainty. This fragmentation poses a significant risk to global growth and stability.
risks.watch_for: Escalation of existing conflicts (e.g., Middle East); new trade disputes; retaliatory tariffs; shifts in global supply chain strategies.
sources: IMF (World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 September Update, September 2026)
World Economic Forum (Chief Economists Outlook, September 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Economic Dependence
risks.summary: The surge in Artificial Intelligence (AI) investment is a significant driver of economic growth, particularly in the US. However, an increasing reliance on this narrow set of drivers presents a downside risk if the AI investment thesis is disrupted.
risks.watch_for: Corporate AI investment spending trends; data center buildouts; AI-related stock valuations; potential disruptions to AI supply chains or technological advancements.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes, September 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 2026)

risks.title: Elevated Energy Prices and Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.summary: The ongoing conflict in the Middle East continues to drive elevated energy prices, which feed into broader inflation through transportation, manufacturing, and food production costs. Supply chain disruptions exacerbate these pressures.
risks.watch_for: Oil and gas prices; Brent crude benchmarks; news on Middle East conflict escalation; reports of supply chain bottlenecks.
sources: IMF (World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 September Update, September 2026)
KPMG (Spring thaw, summer heat: Biannual economic outlook, June 2026)

risks.title: US Fiscal Sustainability and Rising Debt
risks.summary: Growing government deficits and a deteriorating budget trajectory in the US are leading to increased national debt. This raises concerns about fiscal sustainability and the government's ability to finance future demands.
risks.watch_for: Congressional Budget Office (CBO) reports on budget outlook; US Treasury debt issuance levels; discussions on debt ceiling; fiscal stimulus measures.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for, March 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (Got data? Monitoring the US economy, March 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Resilience Amidst Slowing Growth
risks.summary: While the US labor market has shown resilience with job gains keeping pace and a stable unemployment rate, there are concerns about potential headwinds. AI's impact on hiring and a general slowing of job growth could pose risks.
risks.watch_for: Monthly jobs reports (nonfarm payrolls); unemployment rate trends; wage growth data; AI's impact on labor demand.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes, September 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 2026)

risks.title: Sticky Services Inflation and Consumer Spending Moderation
risks.summary: While energy-related inflation pressures may be peaking, sticky services prices continue to contribute to elevated inflation. This, combined with the depletion of fiscal support, could lead to a moderation in consumer spending.
risks.watch_for: Services component of CPI and PCE; consumer spending data (retail sales, personal consumption expenditures); trends in wage growth and housing inflation.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (Economic Outlook / macro themes, September 2026)
KPMG (Spring thaw, summer heat: Biannual economic outlook, June 2026)
IMF (World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 September Update, September 2026)

risks.title: Financial Stability and Liquidity Pressures
risks.summary: Rising global public debt and potential liquidity constraints in developing economies pose risks to financial stability. Central bank actions to combat inflation could also inadvertently expose market fragilities.
risks.watch_for: Global public debt levels; liquidity conditions in emerging markets; signs of stress in financial markets; central bank communication on financial stability.
sources: IMF (World Economic Situation and Prospects 2026 September Update, September 2026)
KPMG (Inflation Forces the Fed's Hand, September 2026)

consensus_note: There is a strong consensus among institutions regarding the persistence of inflation and the necessity for continued monetary policy tightening by the Federal Reserve. Geopolitical fragmentation and trade tensions are also widely flagged as significant downside risks to the global economy. While AI is seen as a growth driver, its increasing importance also introduces a concentration risk. Divergence exists in the precise timing and extent of future rate hikes and the speed at which inflation will return to target.
